title: India's Department of Telecommunications disconnects more than 82 lakh mobile connections that its facial-recognition tool ASTR flagged
summary: The Department of Telecommunications' ASTR facial-recognition tool flags connections that one person took under different names; more than 82 lakh were disconnected after failed re-verification.
account: The Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify and weed out fake, forged and non-bonafide mobile connections. MediaNama reports that ASTR has run since 2021. A Press Information Bureau release from Chennai of 8 May 2023 reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. It said that operators disconnected all of them and handed point-of-sale details to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. MediaNama reported on 9 May 2023 that the department refused its Right to Information request for the ASTR contract as confidential. The Hindu (Press Trust of India, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior official of the department in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected, and operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the Bihar and Jharkhand deactivations as an AI Incident and cites privacy, misidentification and data-protection concerns. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, which the Press Information Bureau posted on 7 August 2025. He said that the department disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The cumulative figure is dated to the posting of that reply. MediaNama reported on 24 July 2026 that a Rajya Sabha reply counted more than 88 lakh disconnections. The department's circular of 17 August 2026 orders operators to match subscriber photographs before issuing a SIM. MediaNama notes that the circular sets no image retention limit and no redress for a faulty facial match. On 9 October 2026 The Hans India reported the minister's statement that India had disconnected over 82 lakh fraudulent mobile connections through ASTR. No source reports an independent evaluation of ASTR's accuracy.

evidence.citation: Vallari Sanzgiri, Why is the contract for telecom department's facial recognition service ASTR confidential?, MediaNama, 9 May 2023. MediaNama has no stake in ASTR and filed its own Right to Information requests; its reporter found that DoT withheld the contract and did not answer questions on data safeguards.
evidence.title: RTI: Telecom dept says info related to ASTR contract is "confidential"
evidence.quote: The work related to ASTR solutions contains confidential information which have personal details of subscribers also.

evidence.citation: Aakriti Bansal, Lowdown: DoT brings facial checks to SIM issuance, orders daily photo downloads, MediaNama, 20 August 2026. MediaNama has no stake in ASTR; its reporter analyzed the DoT circular of 17 August 2026 and reports that ASTR has run since 2021 and that the circular gives a wrongly matched subscriber no grievance route.
evidence.title: Lowdown: DoT brings facial checks to SIM issuance, orders daily photo downloads
evidence.quote: ASTR ran its checks after connections were already active. The circular puts the same face-matching process before a TSP issues the SIM.

display.answer: The 82 lakh and 50,000 figures come from Department of Telecommunications releases on the Press Information Bureau, and The Hans India relays the minister's statement of the 82 lakh figure. The Bihar and Jharkhand figures come from a department official quoted by the Press Trust of India, and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the same deactivations. MediaNama reports from its own Right to Information request and from the circular of 17 August 2026.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: The Department of Telecommunications' ASTR facial-recognition tool flags connections that one person took under different names; more than 82 lakh were disconnected after failed re-verification.
fields.account: The Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify and weed out fake, forged and non-bonafide mobile connections. MediaNama reports that ASTR has run since 2021. A Press Information Bureau release from Chennai of 8 May 2023 reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. It said that operators disconnected all of them and handed point-of-sale details to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. MediaNama reported on 9 May 2023 that the department refused its Right to Information request for the ASTR contract as confidential. The Hindu (Press Trust of India, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior official of the department in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected, and operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the Bihar and Jharkhand deactivations as an AI Incident and cites privacy, misidentification and data-protection concerns. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, which the Press Information Bureau posted on 7 August 2025. He said that the department disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The cumulative figure is dated to the posting of that reply. MediaNama reported on 24 July 2026 that a Rajya Sabha reply counted more than 88 lakh disconnections. The department's circular of 17 August 2026 orders operators to match subscriber photographs before issuing a SIM. MediaNama notes that the circular sets no image retention limit and no redress for a faulty facial match. On 9 October 2026 The Hans India reported the minister's statement that India had disconnected over 82 lakh fraudulent mobile connections through ASTR. No source reports an independent evaluation of ASTR's accuracy.
